sections.h2: What does the Woodbine tax office handle for Camden County owners?
sections.html:
Camden County's tax office takes payments at 200 E 4th Street in Woodbine, and mail goes to PO Box 698. Phone 912-576-3248 between 9 and 5 on weekdays. Appraisal is a different department: the assessors, appointed by the county commissioners, answer valuation questions at 912-576-3241.

One line on the tax commissioner's page deserves attention if you are selling. The office says it has no part in dividing the year's tax between buyer and seller, and that liability for the tax sticks to the owner. Your closing attorney or title company works out the split and asks the office for the figure owed on the parcel.

sections.h2: How is the Camden County bill timed?
sections.html:
Bills leave the county in mid-September, and payment is due 60 days after the mail-out. The recipient is whoever held title on January 1 of that tax year. If you sold afterward, pass the notice to the new owner. Nothing in your mailbox by October 15? Call 912-576-3248.

The Department of Revenue's Camden fact sheet lists December 20 as the standard statewide due date and says a county may shift it or bill in installments. It also gives every taxpayer 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest begins. Camden's own schedule controls, so read the date printed on your statement.

sections.h2: What does a late Camden County bill cost?
sections.html:
Delinquency begins the day after the due date. Interest is the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent a year, a partial month counts as a whole one, and at least $1 is owed (O.C.G.A. 48-5-148). The county's page quotes a monthly figure of 0.7083% from January 2019 as an illustration only.

A flat 5% penalty lands at 120 days overdue, then again at 240, 360 and 480 (O.C.G.A. 48-2-44). Homestead bills of $500 or less escape it, as do new owners who lived outside Georgia, never got a bill and pay within a year.

  • Week after the due date: 30-day lien warning goes out.
  • About a week after that period ends: lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Filing cost, listed at $28.50 to $33.50, joins the bill.
  • After filing, a tax sale can be scheduled.

sections.h2: Can I get my Camden County house back after a tax sale?
sections.html:
Yes, for a limited time. The lien reaches back to the January 1 valuation (O.C.G.A. 48-2-56) and outranks every other lien. Each December 31 the tax commissioner must issue an execution against delinquent accounts (O.C.G.A. 48-3-3), which tells the levying officer to collect or to levy and sell.

Redeeming costs the winning bid, plus any later taxes the buyer covered, plus 20% of that sum for the first year or fraction of a year. Each additional year or fraction adds another 10%. After twelve months the buyer may serve notice to cut off redemption for good (O.C.G.A. 48-4-45 through 48-4-48), and the county notes that the earliest a buyer can take physical control is one year and forty-five days after the deed.

That timeline is why selling before the sale date usually keeps more equity with you than waiting does.

sections.h2: What is the Camden County appeal and refund route?
sections.html:
A Notice of Reassessment starts a 45-day clock. Take the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, and note that the state fact sheet wants it postmarked inside that window. Assessed value is 40% of the January 1 market value, so if market value climbs, assessed value must follow.

Overpayment has its own path. The fact sheet says a written refund request for tax assessed or collected in error can be made within three years of payment.

  • Returns go to the county tax office between January 1 and April 1.
  • Homestead applications are accepted year-round, but April 1 is the cutoff for that year.
  • Skipping the application is treated as waiving the exemption.

sections.h2: Do Kingsland, St. Marys and Woodbine send their own tax bills?
sections.html:
Possibly, and the answer depends on where the house sits. The Department of Revenue's fact sheet explains that cities levy their own ad valorem tax and that the city clerk bills and collects it, unless the city and county have agreed to put everything on one county statement. Only the county tax commissioner can collect motor vehicle tax in any Georgia county.

Ask the Woodbine tax office whether your address carries a separate city bill, and ask the city clerk for any city balance, since an unpaid city tax can hold up a closing just as a county one does.

The same sheet adds a few rules that matter around a purchase. A mobile home must get a county location permit within 30 days of placement and every January 1 to April 1 afterward, and a long-term note secured by real estate must be recorded in the county within 90 days, with intangible recording tax of $1.50 for each $500 of the note.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Camden County's county seat?
sections.html:
Camden was created in 1777 from the St. Thomas and St. Marys parishes and named for the Earl Camden. Its seat sat in St. Marys, the old shipping town, until 1923, when it moved to Woodbine as railways overtook water transport. The Florida Central and Peninsular Railroad had crossed the county in 1893, and U.S. Route 17 followed in 1927.

Rice grew along the Satilla River and Sea Island cotton on Cumberland Island in earlier centuries. The original county was much larger, and it gave up land to form parts of Wayne County in 1808 and 1812 and of Charlton County in 1854.

sections.h2: Why does Kings Bay shape the Camden County housing market?
sections.html:
Camden fills Georgia's southeastern corner, with Glynn County to the north, Nassau County in Florida to the south and Charlton and Brantley counties to the west. Of its 782 square miles, about 22% is water. Kingsland is the biggest city, St. Marys and Woodbine are the others, and Interstate 95 and U.S. 17 run through the county. Cumberland Island National Seashore is part of it.

The Navy chose Kings Bay for a submarine base in 1976, on land the Army had acquired in 1954 for an ocean terminal, and Camden grew fast through the 1980s. Before that, the Gilman paper mill drove the local economy from 1939 until it closed in 2002. More recently, voters overturned the county's option on land for Spaceport Camden in 2022, and the Georgia Supreme Court upheld that result in February 2023.

faqs.q: Does the Woodbine tax office divide the bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner's page says it takes no part in prorating, and liability attaches to the owner. Your closing attorney or title company handles the split, using the balance the office confirms.

faqs.q: I never received a Camden County statement. What now?
faqs.a: Call 912-576-3248. The county asks owners who have nothing by October 15 to get in touch. Interest still builds on a late balance even if the bill never reached you.

faqs.q: How fast does a Camden County lien follow a missed due date?
faqs.a: A 30-day notice is mailed the week after the due date, and the lien is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court about a week after that. The $28.50 to $33.50 filing cost is added to your bill.

faqs.q: After a Camden County tax sale, can the owner redeem?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the buyer's price plus 20% for the first year and 10% for each later year, until the buyer completes the notice steps that bar redemption, which can begin twelve months after the sale.

faqs.q: Is there a late penalty on a small Camden County homestead bill?
faqs.a: The 5% penalty is waived when homestead tax is $500 or less. Interest still applies at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, with a $1 minimum.
